question: An 18-year-old boy who went to the emergency room due to pain and functional impotence in the right knee. After the biopsy study, the diagnosis of osteoblastic osteosarcoma of the distal femur is established. Given the type of tumor and the location, what treatment protocol is usually performed in most cases?

enhanced_information: The standard treatment protocol for osteoblastic osteosarcoma, particularly in the distal femur, typically involves a combination of neoadjuvant chemotherapy, surgical resection, and adjuvant chemotherapy. This approach aims to shrink the tumor preoperatively, allow for limb-sparing surgery, and eliminate any remaining cancer cells postoperatively. Amputation is less common and usually considered only when limb-sparing surgery is not feasible. Radiation therapy is not a standard treatment for osteosarcoma due to its relative radioresistance.
